explain.say: Look around you: a book, a map, fireworks at a festival. They all grew from four inventions made long ago in China: paper, printing, gunpowder and the compass. Let's put them on a timeline, oldest on the left.

explain.say: Here is paper. In 105 CE, an official named Cai Lun improved papermaking. He mashed bark, rags and old fishing nets into pulp and dried it in thin sheets. Before that, people wrote on heavy bamboo or costly silk. Which would you rather carry to school?

explain.say: Next, gunpowder. In the 800s, alchemists, early scientists looking for a medicine for long life, mixed saltpetre, sulphur and charcoal. It flared and banged! It was used first for fireworks and signals, and later for weapons. Surprised?

explain.say: See the book? Printers carved a whole page into a wooden block, inked it and pressed paper on it. The Diamond Sutra from 868 is the oldest printed book with a date. Later, Bi Sheng made single letters you could move around. Why is that faster?

explain.say: Last, the compass. By 1117, Chinese sailors steered with a magnetised needle that points north and south. Super work! Wow: these ideas travelled along trade routes to the whole world, and changed how everyone writes, sails and celebrates.

faq.a: Paper was first made in China around the 2nd century BCE. In 105 CE an official named Cai Lun improved it and reported it to the emperor, so he often gets the credit.

faq.q: What is the oldest printed book?
faq.a: The oldest printed book with a date is the Diamond Sutra, a Buddhist text printed in China in 868 CE. It was found in a cave at Dunhuang and is now in the British Library.
asks: What was the first printed book?

faq.a: Chinese alchemists in the 800s mixed saltpetre, sulphur and charcoal while experimenting, and found it burned fiercely. It was used for fireworks, signals and later weapons.

faq.q: When was the compass first used for navigation?
faq.a: A Chinese book describes sailors using a magnetic compass by 1117 CE. Earlier, magnetic lodestones were used to find directions on land and for fortune-telling.
Movable type means single letters or characters that can be arranged into a page, printed, then rearranged for the next page. Bi Sheng made it from baked clay in the 1040s.

facts: The Diamond Sutra, printed in 868 CE, is the oldest dated printed book.
Bi Sheng invented movable type made of baked clay in the 1040s.
Cai Lun reported his improved papermaking to the emperor in 105 CE.

quiz.say: Which came first: paper, or the compass used at sea?
quiz.why: Paper was improved by 105 CE; sailors used compasses by 1117 CE, about 1,000 years later.

wrong.1: The compass at sea came about 1,000 years after paper.

quiz.say: What was gunpowder first used for?
quiz.why: Its first uses were bright fireworks and signals; weapons came later.

wrong.1: Gunpowder burns far too fiercely for cooking.
wrong.2: Paper is made from plant fibres, not gunpowder.
